title: Simpson's paradox in clinical recovery stratified by severity
what: stratified treatment advantage (+12.0 pp in severe, +5.0 pp in mild; 52% vs 40% severe, 95% vs 90% mild)

reader_questions.question: What is the primary quantitative finding or value?
reader_questions.expected: Treatment outperforms control in BOTH strata: +12 pp in severe (52% vs 40%) and +5 pp in mild (95% vs 90%).

reader_questions.question: Is the difference clearly outside uncertainty or noise?
reader_questions.expected: In the severe stratum (n=250 vs 50) the +12 pp lift is meaningful; in the mild stratum (n=40 treatment) the +5 pp edge has wider uncertainty.

reader_questions.question: What caveat, outlier, control, or subgroup pattern matters?
reader_questions.expected: Classic Simpson's paradox: pooled treatment looks worse (57.9% vs 80.0%) only because 86% of treated patients were severe vs 20% of controls.
